**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 18 (Insurance) already sits at the playbook's **preferred** position on every material term:

| Playbook preferred | Section 18.1 |
|---|---|
| CGL USD 1M/occ, 2M agg | ✅ Matches exactly |
| Professional / E&O USD 2M | ✅ Matches exactly |
| Cyber/privacy USD 5M (data processors) | ✅ Matches exactly |
| Workers' comp as required by law | ✅ Present |
| Certificates on request | ✅ In 18.2 |

The cyber limit is properly calibrated here, since Brightline hosts Customer Data under Sections 15 and 17 — so the USD 5M tier for data-processing vendors is the right trigger, not the fallback USD 2M.

Section 18.2 adds several terms that run in our favour and are better than the model language: reputable insurers, coverage primary to Customer's insurance where customary, advance notice of cancellation or material reduction, and an express statement that insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities (preserving our indemnity and liability rights under Sections 20–21). Coverage also runs for one year post-term, matching the model. Employer's liability of USD 1M is additional cover we did not request.

One minor sub-element noted in the rationale but deliberately not flagged: the cancellation-notice undertaking is qualified by "to the extent available from its insurer" rather than being absolute. Per the classification rules, a missing mechanic of this kind is recorded in the rationale, not raised as a deviation — and pressing it would spend negotiating capital on a clause that otherwise fully meets our ask.
